title: If I were rich
goal: Imagine what you would do if things were different, and give advice with if I were you.

intro.text: Put `-sA` in the if-clause and `-(I)rdI` in the main clause to imagine what isn't so: *Zengin olsam dünyayı gezerdim* (If I were rich, I'd travel the world). Nouns and adjectives go through *olmak*: *zengin olsam*, *param olsa*.

vocab.en: dream, wish; imagination (hayal etmek: to imagine)
to wander, to go around (dünyayı dolaşmak: to travel around the world)

exercises.question: Which sentence tells you that the speaker is **not** rich?

why.1: *Zengin olursam* is a real condition, **if I get rich**: it may still happen.
why.2: *Zengin olunca* means **when I get rich**: the speaker expects it.

exercises.explain: `-sA` in the if-clause and `-(I)rdI` in the main clause: **if I were rich (but I'm not)**.

exercises.en: If I had time, I'd help you.

reject.why: *Varsa* is a real condition, **if I have time**. For an unreal one, *var* goes through *olmak*: *vaktim olsa*.
*Olursa* is a real condition about later. Before *ederdim*, the if-clause takes the plain `-sA`: *olsa*.

exercises.hint: *Var* can't carry this condition. Which verb stands in for it?
exercises.explain: *Vaktim olsa … ederdim*: an unreal present. The speaker has no time.

exercises.label: *gitmek* after an unreal if-clause: I would go, you would go…
exercises.explain: Aorist *gider* (t becomes d before a vowel), then `-DI` and the ending. For **they**, *-ler* usually comes before *-di*: *giderlerdi*.

exercises.prompt: If I were you, I would accept this job.
accept: Senin yerinde olsam bu işi kabul ederdim.
Senin yerinde olsam (ben) bu işi kabul ederim.
Senin yerinde olsam ben bu işi kabul ederdim.
Ben senin yerinde olsam bu işi kabul [ederdim|ederim].
Ben [yerinde|sizin yerinizde|yerinizde] olsam bu işi kabul [ederdim|ederim].

reject.answer: Senin yerinde olursam bu işi kabul ederim.
reject.why: *Olursam* is a real condition, but you can't be in someone else's place. Use *olsam*.

exercises.explain: *Senin yerinde olsam* (if I were in your place) + *kabul ederdim*. The aorist *ederim* is also possible: it imagines more lightly.

accept: If I had wings, I would fly to you.
I would fly to you if I had wings.
If I had wings, I would fly over to you.

exercises.prompt: If we had a boat, we would go to the island.

exercises.en: If you were invisible, what would you do?

exercises.question: *Param olsa bu evi alırdım.* What do you learn about the speaker?
options: They're going to buy this house.

why.1: After a `-sA` clause, *alırdım* isn't a past habit: it means **I would buy**.
why.2: The condition is unreal, so the purchase isn't going to happen.

exercises.explain: *Param olsa … alırdım*: if I had the money, I'd buy it. The speaker doesn't have it.
One-syllable *yap-* takes the aorist `-Ar`: *yapar*. Then `-DI` and the ending, all with back vowels: *yapardım*.

exercises.en: What would you do in my place?
exercises.explain: *Sen olsan*, literally **if it were you**, is the everyday way to ask for advice.

exercises.prompt: If you could fly, where would you go?
exercises.explain: *uç-abil-se-n*: ability, then the conditional. The main clause takes `-(I)rdI`: *giderdin*.

exercises.prompt: Yerinde olsam o işi kabul etmezdim.
accept: If I were you, I would not accept that job.
If I were you, I would not take that job.
If I was you, I would not [accept|take] that job.
I would not [accept|take] that job if I [were|was] you.
If I were in your [place|shoes], I would not [accept|take] that job.

exercises.en: If the weather were nice, we'd go to the sea.
